source.author: verg
source.text: Lamentis gemituque et femineo ululatu tecta fremunt; resonat magnis plangoribus aether, non aliter, quam si immissis ruat hostibus omnis Karthago aut antiqua Tyros, flammaeque furentes culmina perque hominum volvantur perque deorum.
source.text_original: Lamentis gemituque et femineo ululatu / tecta fremunt; resonat magnis plangoribus aether, / non aliter, quam si immissis ruat hostibus omnis / Karthago aut antiqua Tyros, flammaeque furentes / culmina perque hominum volvantur perque deorum.
source.text_english: The roofs resound with wailing and groaning and womanish lament; the sky echoes with great beatings of the breast, no otherwise than if all Karthago or ancient Tyros were falling with enemies let in, and raging flames were rolling over the rooftops and through the houses of men and gods alike.

reuse.text: femineis tantum illa furens ululatibus opstat, obruat Idaeam quantum tuba Martia buxum, fatur et haec:
reuse.text_original: femineis tantum illa furens ululatibus opstat, / obruat Idaeam quantum tuba Martia buxum, / fatur et haec:
reuse.text_english: Only that one, raging, stands in the way with women’s howls, as much as the Martian trumpet drowns the Idaean boxwood pipe; and she says this:
